titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§246–248: The End of Teb-Tenggeri and the Campaign against the Jin
part: §§246–248 — The End of Teb-Tenggeri and the Campaign against the Jin
about: Chinggis Qahan rebukes Father Münlig after Teb-Teṅgeri’s end, and the Qongqotan lose face (§246); in the year of the sheep he rides against the Kitad, the Jin state, with Jebe and Küiküneg in the van, takes Chabchiyal and the passes, and presses Zhongdu (§247); the Altan Qan’s Chancellor Wangjing persuades him to submit, a daughter and treasure are sent out, and Chinggis withdraws (§248). Grammar to watch: converb chains in -žu/-žü carrying the campaign; conditionals in -γ̇asu (Ming 呵 ‘if, when’) that stack before the main clause; the hortative -je/-üje (Ming 咱 ‘let us’); and the Ming glossators’ Chinese place names, which the text treats as Mongol words.

sentences.t: Teb-i talbiγsan qošiliγ-un erüge tuližu eġüden daružu hara sakiγ̇uluγ̇asu
sentences.l: Teb laid-down, tent’s smoke-hole covering, door pressing, men when-made-to-guard,
sentences.i: When they had laid Teb down, covered the tent’s smoke-hole, pressed the door shut and set men to guard it,
sentences.n: The whole chain hangs on one conditional: sakiγ̇uluγ̇asu ‘when (they) had it guarded’ (saki- ‘guard’ + causative -γ̇ul- + -γ̇asu; the Ming 敎守呵 shows the causative with 敎), which is why the English opens ‘When’ and the sentence finishes in the next unit. Teb-i is accusative, so Teb is the one laid down; talbiγsan (Ming 放了的, ‘put down, let go’) is a participle that I render as a finite verb. The Ming does not say why he was laid down or in what state, so read no more than ‘laid down’. The Ming writes 天您 at erüge; I take 您 as a slip for 窗, since the next unit has 天窗 ‘skylight’ for the same word. Nobody is named as the doer; ‘they’ is supplied.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to put down, lay down, let go [放了的]
smoke-hole, skylight of a tent (the Ming has 天您, for 天窗) [天您]
to cover (stem inferred from the Ming 葢) [葢了着]
to press, press down, overcome [壓着]
man, person (printed hara, perhaps qara ‘common, black’) [人]

sentences.t: Γutuγ̇ar süni üdür šira-da ger-ün erüge neġežü beje selte γ̇arčuγ̇u.
sentences.l: third night day yellow-at, tent’s smoke-hole opened, body with went-out.
sentences.i: on the third night and day, at dawn, the tent’s smoke-hole was opened, and he went out, body and all.
sentences.n: beje selte (Ming 身 連) ‘with the body’: he left whole, not as a spirit alone; that much is the Ming’s plain reading. šira-da is ‘at the yellow’ (šira ‘yellow’, Ming 黃行); ‘at dawn’ is my guess at what is yellow here, and the doubt is real. Nobody is named as the one who opened the smoke-hole (neġežü, Ming 開着, ‘having opened’), so I use the passive; the subject of γ̇arčuγ̇u ‘went out’ is Teb, carried over from the last unit. Γutuγ̇ar ‘third’ is the ordinal of γurban ‘three’.

morph.gloss: smoke-hole, skylight of a tent [天窻]
to open (stem inferred from the Ming 開) [開着]

sentences.t: Bolγaγ̇asu maγad Teb in-ü tende bolγaγdaba.
sentences.l: making-sure when, truly, Teb his there was-verified.
sentences.i: When this was looked into, it was truly confirmed of Teb there.
sentences.n: bol- + causative -γa- here carries the Ming 審 ‘examine, make sure’ (the house leaves it unrendered when it means only ‘make’), so bolγaγ̇asu is ‘when it was examined’ and bolγaγdaba (Ming 審實了) ‘was verified’. maγad (Ming 實) is ‘truly’. The text does not say what was verified; I read it as the report about Teb. in-ü tende (Ming 他的 那裏, ‘his, there’) is rendered ‘of Teb there’, and the grammar of that phrase is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to become; with causative -γa-, to make, here with the Ming 審, to examine, make sure [審呵]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; front-vowel form)
to become; with causative -γa-, to make, here with the Ming 審, to examine, verify [審實了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan speaking:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan spoke:
sentences.n: A short frame for the speech that follows. ügülerün is ügüle- ‘to speak’ + -rün ‘while …ing’ (Ming 說). The speech opens at the next unit with Shiratori’s quotation mark on Teb-Teṅgeri.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]

sentences.t: "Teb-Teṅgeri deγ̇ü-ner-tür min-u γar köl kürgegsen-ü tula
sentences.l: "Teb-Tenggeri to-younger-brothers my hand foot having-made-reach on-account-of,
sentences.i: “Because Teb-Tenggeri set my hand and foot upon my younger brothers,
sentences.n: The first of three ‘because’ clauses that all wait for one verb in the third unit; each is closed by tula ‘on account of’ (Ming 上頭). Hard. kürgegsen-ü is kürge- ‘bring to’ (kür- ‘reach’ made causative; the glossary’s stem) + -gsen + genitive, but the Ming 到了的 says only ‘reached’. So I read ‘made my hand and foot reach my younger brothers’, meaning set me physically on them. A different reading takes ‘hand and foot’ as the Chinese idiom 手足 for brothers, so that he ‘brought my own people to my younger brothers’; both come to Teb setting the brothers at odds. I am not certain of either. The speech, Chinggis’s, opens with Shiratori’s mark at Teb-Teṅgeri.

morph.gloss: Teb-Tenggeri, the shaman’s name (Teb + Heaven) [巫名]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to bring to, render (kür- ‘reach’ made causative; uncertain) [到了的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; front-vowel form)
on account of, because of [上頭]

sentences.t: deġü-ner-ün min-u žaγ̇ura oro ügei žeṅgükü-jin tula
sentences.l: younger-brothers-of my between, trace without, slandering-of on-account-of,
sentences.i: and because of the groundless slander between my younger brothers and me,
sentences.n: oro ügei (Ming 痕迹 無, ‘without trace’) I take as ‘groundless’: slander that leaves no trace to point to. Another sense, ‘leaving no room between us’, is possible; the Ming allows both. žaγ̇ura is žaγ̇ur ‘middle’ + dative-locative -a, ‘in the middle, between’ (Ming 其間). žeṅgükü-jin: the stem žeṅgü- ‘slander’ is inferred from the Ming 讒譖, with participle -kü and genitive -jin; ‘the slandering’ is the noun I use. The clause runs on from the last unit and is still waiting for its verb.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to slander, speak ill of (stem inferred from the Ming 讒譖) [讒譖的]
on account of, because of [上頭]

sentences.t: teṅgeri-de ese taγ̇alaγdažu ami-jan beje selte abču oddaba-že" keġebe.
sentences.l: Heaven-by not being-favoured, own-life body with taking was-removed-indeed" said.
sentences.i: was not favoured by Heaven, and was taken away, life and body together,” he said.
sentences.n: This is the main verb of the three clauses: Teb-Teṅgeri ‘was not loved by Heaven’, hence ‘not favoured’ (taγ̇ala-, stem inferred from the Ming 愛, with passive -γda-; the dative teṅgeri-de marks the one who does it). abču ‘taking’ with oddaba (Ming 被惕了) I read as ‘was taken away’, life and body together; odda- is inferred from the Ming 惕 ‘cast off’ and the exact verb is uncertain. ese (Ming 不) negates a past act. Shiratori closes the quotation at oddaba-že; keġebe ‘said’ follows it.

morph.gloss: to love, favour (stem inferred from the Ming 愛) [被愛着]
to be cast off, taken away (stem inferred from the Ming 惕) [被惕了也者︀]
sentence-final particle: it is so, indeed

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Müṅlig ečige-ji tende doṅγodurun
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Münlig father-ACC there when-rebuking:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, rebuking Father Münlig there:
sentences.n: ečige-ji ‘father’ (Ming 父 行) is the title the house writes ‘Father Münlig’, in the accusative after a vowel. tende ‘there’ means on the spot. doṅγod- here has the Ming 恠責 ‘blame, rebuke’; in §244 the same stem was glossed 作聲 ‘make a sound’, so I follow the Ming at each place. -urun (linking vowel + -run) is ‘while’. No colon is printed, but the rebuke that follows opens with Shiratori’s mark.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to rebuke, find fault with (Ming 恠責) [恠責]

sentences.t: "köġüd-ü-ġen abüri ülü idqan deṅgečen sedkikün bolun Teb-Teṅgeri-jin teriġün-dür kürbe ta.
sentences.l: "own-sons conduct not checking, equal-being thinkers becoming, Teb-Tenggeri’s head-at reached you.
sentences.i: “You did not check your own sons’ conduct; becoming men who thought themselves equals, you came to Teb-Tenggeri’s head.
sentences.n: A hard sentence, and the Ming’s words are more certain than the sense. ülü idqan ‘not checking’ (idqa- inferred from the Ming 止當 ‘hold back’); deṅgečen sedkikün bolun ‘becoming thinkers of equality’ (Ming 齊等 想每 做); teriġün-dür kürbe ‘reached to the head’ (Ming 頭行 到了). teriġün is head, front or chief, so the clause may say they rose up to Teb-Teṅgeri’s level, or took the lead with him, or pushed ahead of the Qahan; I can’t tell which, and ‘thought themselves equals’ does not say equal to whom. ta ‘you’ (plural, respectful) ends it. köġüd-ü-ġen is köġün + plural -d + a linking vowel -ü- (not a genitive, as the glossary has it) + reflexive -ġen, ‘one’s own sons’; the conduct belongs to them by juxtaposition. The opening quotation is Shiratori’s.

morph.gloss: linking vowel before the reflexive-possessive after the plural -d (not a genitive)
to check, hold back (stem inferred from the Ming 止當) [止當]

sentences.t: Tan-u teimü aburi uqaγsan böġesü Žamuqa, Altan, Qučar-tan-u josutan bolγaγdaqun büleġei ta"
sentences.l: Your such conduct having-understood if-it-were, Jamuqa, Altan, Quchar-and-others’ rightly being-made you-would-have-been"
sentences.i: If you had understood such conduct of yours, you would have been dealt with rightly, as Jamuqa, Altan, Quchar and the others were,”
sentences.n: A counterfactual: uqaγsan böġesü ‘if (you) had understood’ (Ming 省了 有呵) and büleġei, the past in -leġei, ‘you would have been’. The hard part is josutan bolγaγdaqun (Ming 道理有的每 被做了), ‘those with right, made so’: I give ‘dealt with rightly’. Quchar-tan-u joins Qučar with -tan ‘and the like’ (Ming 等) and a genitive, so the three men are named as the standard of comparison. What became of those three is not said here and I do not supply it. Shiratori’s closing mark falls at ta.

morph.gloss: you (plural, respectful, oblique stem tan-) [您的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
Quchar, a man’s name [人名 等的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to become; with causative -γa-, to make [被做了您]
past tense: was, would have been

sentences.t: keġežü Müṅlig ečige-ji duṅγodču doṅγodun baražu
sentences.l: saying, Münlig father-ACC rebuking, rebuking, finishing
sentences.i: Having said this, he rebuked Father Münlig through to the end,
sentences.n: The doubled doṅγod- (converbs -ču and -un, both Ming 恠責) with bara- ‘end’ (Ming 了) means rebuking at length until done. Shiratori spells the stem both duṅγod- and doṅγod-. The chain ends here: the next unit opens a new speech.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to rebuke, find fault with [恠責着]
to rebuke, find fault with [恠責了着]

sentences.t: "žiči manaγaru ügülegsen-i üdeši hudaruγ̇asu üde-jin ügülegsen-i manaγar hudaruγ̇asu hičere maqa keġegdekü.
sentences.l: "then morning said-ACC by-evening if-broken, evening-of said-ACC next-morning if-broken, shame perhaps to-be-called.
sentences.i: “Then if what was said in the morning is broken by evening, and what was said in the evening is broken by the next morning, would that not be called shame?
sentences.n: A rhetorical question: hičere maqa keġegdekü (Ming 羞耻 莫不 被稱的), ‘would it not be called shame’, with maqa (Ming 莫) as ‘perhaps (not)’ as elsewhere in the text. hudar- (Ming 解折 ‘break up, undo’) is used of a spoken word. The two clauses balance: manaγaru ‘in the morning’ (Ming 早晨) against manaγar ‘next morning’ (Ming 明早), and üdeši ‘by evening’ (a noun üdeši in the glossary, perhaps üde + directional -ši) against üde-jin ‘of the evening’. hudaruγ̇asu is hudar- + a linking vowel -u- + -γ̇asu. Shiratori’s opening mark is at žiči (Ming 郤 ‘then, but’); he closes at Teli, two units on.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
evening, toward evening (noun; here ‘by evening’) [晩夕]
to break up, undo (a word given) [解折呵]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to break up, undo (a word given) [解折呵]

sentences.t: Ele urida üge baraγdaluγ̇a-že.
sentences.l: Only formerly word was-settled.
sentences.i: Yet the earlier word stood settled.
sentences.n: Ele (Ming 但 ‘only, yet’) sets up a contrast; baraγdaluγ̇a-že is bara- ‘end’ + passive + past (Ming 定了了來罷, ‘was fixed’), so ‘was settled’. My reading of the logic: Chinggis cannot undo what he once promised, and the next unit closes the matter. The text does not say what the word was, and I do not fill it in.

morph.gloss: to end, finish, be settled [定了了來罷]
sentence-final particle: it is so, indeed

sentences.t: Teli" keġen sojurγažu žiči žariraba.
sentences.l: that-matter" saying, favour-showing, then anger-calmed.
sentences.i: Let that matter stand,” he said; showing favour, he then grew calm.
sentences.n: Teli (Ming 那事, ‘that matter’) is a bare noun; the verb ‘let (it) stand’ is mine, taken from what the last unit and the calming that follows imply. The Ming says only ‘that matter’. sojurγažu (Ming 恩賜着 ‘bestowing favour’) with žiči (Ming 遂 ‘thereupon’) and žarira- ‘to calm down’ (Ming 息怒, ‘anger subsided’). Shiratori closes the quotation, opened at žiči in the unit before last, at Teli; `i` therefore supplies only the closing mark here.

sentences.t: "Alus aburi-jan tataγsan böġesü Müṅlig ečige-jin uruγ-tur ken deṅgečekün büleġei" keġebe.
sentences.l: "beyond own-conduct having-drawn-in if-it-had-been, Münlig father-of descendants-to who equal would-have-been" said.
sentences.i: “If they had drawn in their own conduct where it overstepped, who would have been the equal of Father Münlig’s descendants?” he said.
sentences.n: alus (Ming 隔越, ‘step across, overstep’) is the word the house renders ‘beyond(?)’; tata- is ‘draw in, rein in’ (Ming 縮 ‘shorten’). I read this as a softening after the rebuke: the family’s one fault is overreach, and without it they would have had no equal. ken deṅgečekün büleġei is ‘who would have been an equal’ (Ming 誰 齊等每 有來), and the dative uruγ-tur (Ming 子孫 行) is ‘to the descendants’: the one to whom the equal is compared, so ‘equal of Father Münlig’s descendants’. Shiratori puts an opening mark at Alus and a closing mark after büleġei, then keġebe.

morph.gloss: conduct, character, temper [德性 自的行]
to draw in, rein in [縮了]
to be equal, match (stem inferred from the Ming 齊等; compare the adjective deṅgečen) [齊等每]
past tense: was, would have been

sentences.t: Teb-Teṅgeri-ji ügei bolγaγ̇ad Qoṅγotan čirai žibturažuγ̇ui-že.
sentences.l: Teb-Tenggeri-ACC non-existing having-made, Qongqotan face dwindled-has.
sentences.i: They made an end of Teb-Tenggeri, and the Qongqotan lost face.
sentences.n: Outside any quotation. ügei bolγa- (‘make non-existent’, with the Ming 無 做了) is ‘do away with’; the subject is not named and ‘they’ is supplied. Teb-Teṅgeri-ji is accusative. Qoṅγotan is, in the Ming, only a tribal name (種名); čirai (Ming 顏色, ‘colour of the face’) with žibtura- (Ming 消減, ‘diminish’) gives ‘their face dwindled’, which I put as ‘lost face’. -žuγ̇ui is a perfect (Ming 有) and -že the final particle.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to become; with causative -γa-, to make [做了]
to diminish, dwindle [消減了有 也者︀]
sentence-final particle: it is so, indeed

sentences.t: Teġün-ü qoina Čiṅgis Qaγan qonin žil Kitad irgen-dür morilaba.
sentences.l: That-of after Chinggis Qaγan sheep year Kitad people-to mounted.
sentences.i: After that, in the year of the sheep, Chinggis Qahan rode out against the Kitad people.
sentences.n: Kitad is glossed 金國 by the Ming, ‘the Jin state’: the Ming reader’s name for the realm, where the Mongol text uses the people’s name. qonin žil is the sheep year of the twelve-year cycle (Ming 羊 年); the text gives no number, so I name no year. morilaba is mori ‘horse’ + -la- + past (Ming 上馬了 ‘mounted’), so ‘rode out’. irgen-dür is a dative of the target (Ming 行), hence ‘against’.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; front-vowel form)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
the Kitad (Khitan), here the Jin state and its people [金國]

sentences.t: Füžü-ji abču Hünegen dabā-γ̇ar dabažu Šuandefü-ji abču
sentences.l: Fuzhou-ACC taking, Fox pass-by crossing, Xuande-prefecture-ACC taking,
sentences.i: He took Fuzhou, crossed over by way of the Fox Pass, and took Xuande Prefecture,
sentences.n: Three Chinese place names from the Ming: Füžü (撫州, Fuzhou), Hünegen (Ming 野狐, ‘wild fox’) with dabā ‘pass’ (the Ming’s 嶺 is ‘ridge’), and Šuandefü (宣德府, Xuande prefecture). I treat hünegen as the animal and the pass as ‘Fox Pass’; it may be a name taken over from Chinese. dabā-γ̇ar is the instrumental ‘by, through’ (Ming 依着); daba- is ‘cross a pass’ (Ming 越). Both prefectures are accusative (Ming 行).

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to cross over a pass [越着]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.t: Žebe Küiküneg baγ̇atur qojar-i maṅlai ilebe.
sentences.l: Jebe Küiküneg hero two-ACC vanguard sent.
sentences.i: He sent the two heroes, Jebe and Küiküneg, ahead as the vanguard.
sentences.n: qojar-i (Ming 兩箇 行) is ‘the two of them’ in the accusative, standing after the names; baγ̇atur is ‘hero, brave man’ (Ming 勇士). maṅlai is ‘forefront’ (Ming 首先 ‘first’), and ilebe (Ming 敎去了) ‘sent’. I keep the second name as Shiratori prints it, Küiküneg (Han 古亦古捏克); I make no guess at another form.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.t: Čabčijal kürčü Čabčijal dabaγ̇an-i bekilegdežü tende Žebe ügülerün:
sentences.l: Chabchiyal having-reached, Chabchiyal pass-ACC being-guarded, there Jebe speaking:
sentences.i: On reaching Chabchiyal, they found the Chabchiyal pass guarded. There Jebe said:
sentences.n: Čabčijal is the Juyong Pass (Ming 居庸關). bekilegdežü is bekile- ‘guard, defend’ (stem inferred from the Ming 守禦) with passive -gde-, ‘being guarded’ (Ming 被守禦着); who guards it is not said, and ‘they found’ is supplied. The accusative on dabaγ̇an-i (Ming 嶺行) is the Mongol way of marking the object of the guarding. ügülerün ‘while speaking’ leads into Jebe’s plan.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to guard, defend (stem inferred from the Ming 守禦) [被守禦着]

sentences.t: "An-i üdüžü ködölgežü ireġülün tende sorija" keġežü qariba.
sentences.l: "them-ACC luring, setting-in-motion, making-come, there let-us-try" saying, turned-back.
sentences.i: “Let us lure them, stir them up, draw them on, and try them there,” he said, and they turned back.
sentences.n: Jebe’s plan is a chain of three converbs ending in a hortative: üdü- ‘lure’ (stem inferred from the Ming 引誘), ködöl- ‘move’ + causative -ge-, ‘set in motion’ (Ming 動着), ire- + causative -ġül- ‘make come’ (Ming 敎來), then sori- + hortative -ja ‘let us try’ (Ming 試咱). An-i is the third-person plural object (Ming 他每行). The turning back that follows reads as the lure itself, but the text does not say it was feigned. Shiratori marks both ends of the quotation.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to lure, entice (stem inferred from the Ming 引誘) [引誘着]
to move, set out; with causative -ge-, to set in motion [動着]

sentences.t: Qariγdažu Kitad-un čeriġüd nekeje keġen
sentences.l: Being-turned-back Kitad’s troops let-us-pursue saying,
sentences.i: As they turned back, the Kitad troops said, “Let us pursue them,”
sentences.n: Qariγdažu is qari- ‘turn back’ + passive -γda- (Ming 被囘着, ‘being turned back’). Who turns whom is not plain; I read it as the raiders’ turning, since the Kitad then pursue. nekeje is neke- ‘pursue’ (Ming 追襲) + hortative. Shiratori prints no quotation marks here; `i` supplies both, closing at keġen.

morph.gloss: the Kitad (Khitan), here the Jin state [金(國)的]
to pursue, attack on the heels [追襲咱]

sentences.t: Čülge aγ̇ula bütetele nekežü aiši.
sentences.l: Plain mountain until-full, pursuing, came.
sentences.i: and they came on in pursuit until plains and mountains were full of them.
sentences.n: Čülge (Ming 川) I take as ‘plain’, though 川 can also be a river valley; aγ̇ula is ‘mountain’. bütetele is büte- ‘be full, complete’ (Ming 塞滿) + -tele ‘until’. aiši (Ming 來也) is ai- ‘come’ + -ši, which the glossary reads as a present, ‘is coming’; I put it as ‘came’ in the narrative and cannot confirm the ending. The stem recurs as aisu- in aisunqun below.

sentences.t: Šuandefü-jin qošiγ̇un-a kürčü Žebe qoinaγši hurba.
sentences.l: Xuande-prefecture’s beak-at having-reached, Jebe backward turned.
sentences.i: Reaching the edge of Xuande, Jebe wheeled right round.
sentences.n: qošiγ̇un is literally ‘beak’ (Ming 觜): a point, tip or edge, and ‘at the edge of’ is my reading of 觜行. qoinaγši is qoina ‘behind’ + a directional (Ming 往後 ‘toward the rear’); hurba (Ming 翻了, ‘turned over’) I take as hur- + -ba, a stem I cannot fix (the glossary has hurbažu from hurba- ‘turn over’, which may be the same verb). The sense is that he turned about, face to the pursuers.

morph.gloss: to turn over, wheel round (stem uncertain) [翻了]

sentences.t: Tatažu dobtulžu sundurču aisunqun dain-i daruba.
sentences.l: Wheeling, charging, in-succession those-who-came enemy-ACC overcame.
sentences.i: Wheeling and charging, he beat the enemy as they came on strung out.
sentences.n: tata- is ‘draw’, here of the reins (Ming 掉 ‘turn about’), hence ‘wheeling’; dobtul- is ‘charge’ (Ming 衝); sundurču (Ming 陸續) is ‘one after another’. aisunqun is ‘those who come’ (Ming 來的每); aisunqun is aisu- ‘come’ (the glossary’s stem) + a participle -nqun; the ending is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to draw, pull, of reins, to wheel about [掉着]
to come one after another, straggle [陸續]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan γol čerig daručažu Kitad-i ködölgežü
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan centre army following-together, Kitad-ACC setting-in-motion,
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan, with the centre army pressing on together, drove the Kitad before him,
sentences.n: γol čerig is ‘the centre army’ (Ming 中 軍). daručažu is daruča- ‘press hard, pursue closely’ (the glossary’s stem; perhaps daru- ‘press’ + -ča- ‘together’) + -žu (Ming 相隨着, ‘following along’): the whole host moving as one. ködöl- ‘move’ + causative -ge-, ‘set in motion’ (Ming 推動着 ‘push’) is my ‘drove before him’. The converb chain runs into the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
to press hard, pursue closely (perhaps daru- ‘press’ + -ča- ‘together’) [相隨着]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to move, set out; with causative -ge-, to set in motion, push [推動着]

sentences.t: Qara-Kitad-un Žürčed-ün Žuin-u erekün omoγ-un čeriġüd-i daružu
sentences.l: Black-Kitad’s, Jurchen’s, Juin’s brave bold troops-ACC overcoming,
sentences.i: defeating the brave and bold troops of the Qara-Kitad, the Jurchen and the Juin,
sentences.n: Three peoples in the genitive: Qara-Kitad-un (Ming 契丹), Žürčed-ün (女眞, the Jurchen; the -d is probably a plural, as in Kitad), Žuin-u (種名, only ‘a tribe name’ in the Ming, so ‘Juin’ is a bare transliteration). erekün omoγ-un (Ming 勇 猛的) ‘brave and bold’ modifies the troops; the stem omoγ ‘bold’ is taken from the Ming and uncertain.

morph.gloss: the Qara-Kitad, Black Kitad [契丹 的]
the Jurchen (the -d is probably a plural, as in Kitad) [女眞 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
daring, bold (adjective; the ending is uncertain) [勇]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.t: Čabčijal-a kürtele hunžiγ̇u baitala kidužu
sentences.l: Chabchiyal-to until, rotten-wood heap-like, killing,
sentences.i: and killing them in heaps like rotten logs all the way to Chabchiyal,
sentences.n: The simile is the Ming’s: 爛木 堆般 for hunžiγ̇u baitala, ‘rotten wood, heap-like’. baitala is uncertain (perhaps bai- ‘be, lie’ + -tala ‘until, as’); the Ming meaning guides the English. kidu- is ‘kill’ (Ming 殺), and kürtele ‘as far as’ is kür- + -tele.

morph.gloss: Chabchiyal, the Juyong Pass [居庸關(行)]

sentences.t: Čabčijal-un qaγ̇alγa Žebe abču dabaγ̇ad buližu dabažu
sentences.l: Chabchiyal-of gate Jebe taking, passes seizing, crossing,
sentences.i: Jebe took the gate of Chabchiyal, seized the passes and crossed over,
sentences.n: qaγ̇alγa is ‘gate, barrier’ (Ming 關), the pass itself. dabaγ̇ad (Ming 嶺每) is the plural of daba (the glossary’s lemma; dabaγan above is the same word); buli- is ‘seize, snatch’ (Ming 奪). The actor is Jebe; the Qahan is the subject again in the next unit.

morph.gloss: Chabchiyal, the Juyong Pass [居庸(關)的]
to cross over a pass [越着]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Šira-Deg-tür baγ̇uba.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan Shira-Deg-at alighted.
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan encamped at Shira-Deg.
sentences.n: Šira-Deg is a place the Ming glosses as 龍虎臺名, ‘a place called Dragon-Tiger Terrace’; I leave the Mongol name as printed. baγ̇u- is ‘descend, dismount, make camp’ (Ming 下了).

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [(太祖︀)]
Shira-Deg, a place (Dragon-Tiger Terrace) [龍虎臺名(行)]

sentences.t: Žundu-ji eġerežü qotod qotod balaγad-tur čeriġüd iležü eġereġülbe.
sentences.l: Zhongdu-ACC attacking, cities cities towns-to troops sending, had-attack.
sentences.i: While attacking Zhongdu, he sent troops against city after city and against the towns, and had them attack.
sentences.n: Žundu-ji is accusative. The Ming glosses it 大都 ‘Great Capital’, while the Han transcription 中都 is ‘Central Capital’; I follow the Han and write Zhongdu. qotod and balaγad are plurals (Ming 城子每 for both); I keep the two words apart as ‘city’ and ‘town’, though the Ming does not. iležü eġereġülbe is ‘sending, made (them) attack’, with causative -ġül-.

morph.gloss: Zhongdu, the Central Capital [大都︀ 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
enclosure; walled town, city (compare qoton ‘pen’ in the glossary; here the Ming 城子) [城子每]
enclosure; walled town, city (compare qoton ‘pen’ in the glossary; here the Ming 城子) [城子每]
towns, cities (plural in -d; the singular balaγasun occurs in this part) [城(每)行]

sentences.t: Žebe-ji Duṅžaṅ balaγasun eġereġülün ilebe.
sentences.l: Jebe-ACC Dongchang town having-attack-made, sent.
sentences.i: He sent Jebe to attack the city of Dongchang.
sentences.n: eġereġülün ilebe is ‘sent (him) to make it be attacked’, the causative -ġül- here in its usual ‘send X to do’ sense. Duṅžaṅ (Ming 郡名, a commandery’s name, 東昌) is Dongchang; I do not place it further.

morph.gloss: Jebe, a man’s name [人名 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)

sentences.t: Duṅžaṅ balaγasun-dur kürčü eġerežü abun jadažu qarižu
sentences.l: Dongchang town-at having-reached, attacking, taking being-unable, turning-back,
sentences.i: Reaching the city of Dongchang, he attacked it but could not take it, and turned back,
sentences.n: abun jadažu is ‘taking, being unable’: ab- ‘take’ with converb -un and jada- ‘be unable’ (Ming 不能着). So ‘attacked but could not take’. This unit and the next two are one sentence cut at its converbs.

sentences.t: žirγoγ̇an qonoγ γažar-a kürčü genedgežü žiči qarin tataγ̇ad
sentences.l: six night-stop land-to having-reached, to-take-unawares, then back drawing,
sentences.i: reaching a place six night-stops off, and, to catch the enemy unawares, wheeled back,
sentences.n: žirγoγ̇an qonoγ (Ming 六 宿) is ‘six nights’, that is six night-camps’ march; γažar-a (Ming 地行) ‘to a place’. genedge- is inferred from the Ming 使不意 ‘cause to be unprepared’, hence ‘take unawares’. qarin tataγ̇ad is ‘turning back, wheeling’, tata- as in the unit above. ‘The enemy’ is supplied.

morph.gloss: to take unawares (stem inferred from the Ming 使不意) [使不意]
to draw, pull, here, to wheel about [掉]

sentences.t: qar kötölten süni düliligežü gened büküi-dür kürčü Duṅžaṅ balaγasu abuγ̇ai.
sentences.l: each-man spare-horse-having, night double-marching, unawares being-in, having-reached, Dongchang town took.
sentences.i: Each man leading a spare horse, they rode through the night at double pace, arrived while the enemy was off guard, and took the city of Dongchang.
sentences.n: qar is ‘hand’ (printed qar), here ‘each man’ (Ming 每人). kötölten is kötöl ‘led spare horse’ (Ming 牽一匹從馬) + -ten ‘those having’. düliligežü (Ming 兼行着) is a march at double stages. gened büküi-dür (Ming 不 意 間) is ‘while (they were) unaware’, with the defenders left unnamed; the stem gened is uncertain. abuγ̇ai is ab- ‘take’ + a past ending (Ming 要了).

morph.gloss: to march at double stages (stem inferred from the Ming 兼行) [兼行着]

sentences.t: Žebe Duṅžaṅ balaγasan-i abču qarižu irežü Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur neilebe.
sentences.l: Jebe Dongchang town-ACC taking, turning-back, coming, Chinggis Qaγan-to joined.
sentences.i: Jebe took the city of Dongchang, came back, and rejoined Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: neile- is ‘join, unite’ (Ming 相合), here ‘rejoined’. Shiratori prints balaγasan-i, with a for u, but the Han 巴剌中合速泥 is balaγasuni, so I read the same word as in the units above, in the accusative.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Žundu-ji eġeregderün Altan Qān-u jeke nojan Waṅgiṅ Čiṅsaṅ Altan Qān-a duradγarun:
sentences.l: Zhongdu-ACC when-being-attacked, Altan Qan’s great officer Wangjing Chancellor Altan Qan-to reminding:
sentences.i: While Zhongdu was under attack, the Altan Qan’s great officer, Chancellor Wangjing, put it to the Altan Qan:
sentences.n: eġeregderün is eġere- ‘attack’ + passive -gde- + -rün ‘while’ (Ming 被攻時). Altan Qān (Ming 金皇帝) is the ruler of the Jin; altan is ‘gold’. Čiṅsaṅ (Han 丞相; the Ming says only (官名), ‘an official title’) is the Chinese title ‘chancellor’ written in the Mongol way, and Waṅgiṅ (Han 王京; Ming 人名) the man’s name; jeke nojan is ‘great officer’ (Ming 大 官人). duradγa- is ‘bring to mind, mention’ (Ming 提說), here ‘put it to’.

morph.gloss: Zhongdu, the Central Capital [大都︀ 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to bring to mind, mention, raise [提說]

sentences.t: "Teṅgeri γažar-un žajaγ̇an čaγ jeke oro jeġüdgeküi čaγ(u)-u kürbe.
sentences.l: "Heaven Earth’s fate time, great seat changing-over time-of has-reached.
sentences.i: “The time of the decree of Heaven and Earth has come, the time when the great throne changes hands.
sentences.n: The Chancellor speaks of the throne changing hands without naming who gives and who takes. Teṅgeri γažar-un is ‘of Heaven and Earth’ (Ming 天 地的) and žajaγ̇an ‘fate, decree’ (Ming 命). oro, glossed 位子 ‘seat’, is the word that meant ‘trace’ in §246; here its other sense, ‘place, throne’. jeġüdgeküi (Ming 交代 ‘hand over, take turns’) has an inferred stem. čaγ(u)-u keeps Shiratori’s bracketed linking vowel; kürbe (Ming 敢到了) is ‘has indeed come’. The speech opens with Shiratori’s mark on Teṅgeri and runs to medegdekü.

morph.gloss: to hand over, change over (stem inferred from the Ming 交代) [交代]
genitive: of (with Shiratori’s bracketed linking vowel (u), as in -(n)u)

sentences.t: Monγol maši küčütej-e irežü
sentences.l: Mongols very strength-having-to came,
sentences.i: The Mongols have come, very strong,
sentences.n: küčütej-e is küčü ‘strength’ (Ming 氣力) + -tei ‘having’ + -e, which the Ming glosses 行 ‘to’. I take it as ‘being strong’; ‘to the strong ones’ is also possible. maši (Ming 好生) is ‘very’. Monγol is glossed 達達 (‘Tatars’) by the Ming glossators, their word for the Mongols.

sentences.t: bidan-u erekün omoγ-un Qara-Kitad-un Žürčed-ün Žuin-u erkid čeriġüd-i daružu bürektele kidužuγ̇ul.
sentences.l: our brave bold Black-Kitad’s Jurchen’s Juin’s leading troops-ACC overcoming, until-extinct killed-have.
sentences.i: and have overcome our leading troops, the brave and bold Qara-Kitad, Jurchen and Juin, and killed them to the last.
sentences.n: erkid + noun is ‘leading …’ (the house rendering; Ming 緊要的 ‘of key importance’). bidan-u is ‘our’, inclusive, the oblique stem bidan- + genitive (Ming 咱的). The same pair erekün omoγ-un, ‘brave and bold’, was used above of the same three peoples’ troops. bürektele is ‘until finished’: bürek- is inferred from the Ming 滅絕 ‘wiped out’, with -tele. kidužuγ̇ul is kidu- ‘kill’ + a perfect (Ming 殺了有), ‘have killed’.

morph.gloss: we, us (inclusive, oblique stem bidan-) [咱的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
daring, bold (adjective; the ending is uncertain) [勇]
the Qara-Kitad, Black Kitad [契丹 的]
the Jurchen (the -d is probably a plural, as in Kitad) [女眞 的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
power, authority (stem uncertain; sense from the Ming) [緊要的(每)]
plural: the powerful ones, the leaders
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to be finished, wiped out (stem inferred from the Ming 滅絕) [滅絕]

sentences.t: Itegeltü Čabčijal-i ber buližu abčuγ̇ui.
sentences.l: Reliable Chabchiyal-ACC even seizing, have-taken.
sentences.i: They have even seized Chabchiyal, which we relied on.
sentences.n: Itegeltü is itegel ‘trust’ + -tü ‘having’ (Ming 可倚仗有的, ‘something to rely on’); standing before Čabčijal it reads as ‘trusted Chabchiyal’. ber (Ming 也) is ‘even, also’. abčuγ̇ui (Ming 要了有) is a perfect, ‘have taken’.

morph.gloss: Chabchiyal, the Juyong Pass [居庸關行]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.t: Edöġe bida basa čeriġüd žasažu γarγaγ̇asu basa moṅγol-a duraγdaγ̇asu qalaγ̇ar
sentences.l: Now we again troops organizing if-go-out, again Mongols-by if-overcome, certainly
sentences.i: If we now organize our troops again and march out, and are again beaten by the Mongols, then surely
sentences.n: Two conditionals in -γ̇asu (Ming 呵 ‘if’) stacked before the main clause, which is in the next unit. žasa- is ‘put in order’ (Ming 整治); γarγa- is γar- ‘go out’ with a causative -γa-, ‘lead out, march out’ (Ming 出去). Shiratori prints duraγdaγ̇asu, but the Han 荅舌魯黑荅 is daruγda-, so the stem is daru- ‘overcome’ + passive; I read the printed -ra- as a slip for -ru-. Moṅγol-a (Ming 達達行) is a dative of the agent, ‘by the Mongols’. qalaγ̇ar is ‘certainly’ (Ming 必然).

morph.gloss: to put in order, organize [整治着]

sentences.t: balaγad balaγad-tur(i)-jan butaraqun tede.
sentences.l: towns, towns-in-own scattering, they.
sentences.i: they will scatter, town by town, each to his own.
sentences.n: tede (Ming 他每) is ‘they’, the people of the towns, whom the Ming leaves unspecified. balaγad is the plural of balaγasun; the second balaγad-tur(i)-jan has a dative -tur with a reflexive (i)jan, ‘in their own’, in the way the house writes mör-tür(i)-jen. butara- is ‘scatter, rout’ (Ming 潰散).

morph.gloss: towns, cities (plural in -d; the singular balaγasun occurs in this part) [城子(每)]
towns, cities (plural in -d; the singular balaγasun occurs in this part) [城子(每)裏自的行]

sentences.t: Žiči bidan-a quraγ̇uluγ̇asu ülü bolun bidan-dur daisun bolžu ülü nököčekün tede.
sentences.l: Then us-to if-gathered, not willing, us-to enemy making, not accompanying, they.
sentences.i: And if we then call them in to us, they will not agree; they will turn against us and refuse to be our companions.
sentences.n: bidan-a quraγ̇uluγ̇asu is ‘if (they) are made to gather to us’ (qura- ‘gather’ + causative -γ̇ul- + -γ̇asu; Ming 收呵). ülü bolun (Ming 不 肯) is ‘not agreeing’, with bolun glossed 肯 ‘willing’. daisun bolžu is ‘becoming an enemy’ (Ming 反 做着, ‘turning rebel’). nököčekün (Ming 做伴) is ‘one who would accompany’; with ülü it is ‘would not be companions’. The last word tede ‘they’ is the same people as before.

morph.gloss: to become, to be, here, to be willing [肯]
to accompany, be a companion [做伴]

sentences.t: Altan Qān-i sojurγaγ̇asu Moṅγol-un Qān-dur edöġed-tür elsen ejetüje.
sentences.l: Altan Qan-ACC if-favouring, Mongols’ Qan-to now submitting let-us-take-counsel.
sentences.i: If the Altan Qan will deign to allow it, let us now take counsel to submit to the Mongol Qan.
sentences.n: A doubtful opening. sojurγaγ̇asu (Ming 恩賜呵, ‘if he bestows favour’) is a polite formula, ‘if he deigns’, but it stands after an accusative, Altan Qān-i, which is odd; the Ming 金皇帝(行) 恩賜呵 has the same shape. My reading is that the Altan Qan is asked to allow the plan. The other reading, ‘if (the Mongol Qan) shows favour to the Altan Qan’, is not excluded. elsen is else- ‘submit’ (the glossary’s stem; Ming 歸附) + converb -n; ejetüje is eje ‘counsel’ + -tü- + hortative -je (Ming 商量咱). edöġed-tür (Ming 如今裏) is ‘now’ with a dative ending.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 歸附) [歸附]

sentences.t: Eje-dür orožu Monγol-i ičuγ̇asu ičuγaγsan-u qoina basa busu sedkil bida tende ejetüldüd-že.
sentences.l: Counsel-in entering, Mongols-ACC if-made-to-withdraw, withdrawn-of after, again other thought we there let-us-confer.
sentences.i: Going along with this counsel, if the Mongols are made to withdraw, then after they have withdrawn let us turn our thoughts to something else and take counsel there together.
sentences.n: My reading is that this finishes the plan begun above: agree to submit, get the Mongols to withdraw, then think again. eje-dür orožu (Ming 商量 裏 入着) is ‘entering into the counsel’, joining it. Moṅγol-i ičuγ̇asu (Ming 達達行 退呵) has an accusative, so I read it as ‘if the Mongols are made to withdraw’ (compare ičuγ̇ažu in the glossary, a causative); the intransitive ‘if the Mongols withdraw’ is the other reading. busu sedkil (Ming 別 想) is ‘another thought’. ejetüldüd-že is eje + -tü- + reciprocal -ldü- + plural -d + -že (Ming 商量 也者): the hortative, ‘let us confer together’. The stems of ičuγ̇asu (ič-), ičuγaγsan (ičuγa- ‘turn back’) and ičuba (ič-) follow the glossary and are uncertain; the Ming gives 退 each time.

morph.gloss: accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred; Ming 退) [退呵]
conditional-temporal: if, when (linking vowel -u- + -γ̇asu; with the accusative Monγol-i perhaps causative ‘make withdraw’)
to turn back, drive back, withdraw [退了的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to take counsel [商量 也者︀]
sentence-final particle: it is so, indeed

sentences.t: Moṅγol-un ba ere aγta γažar heġüšiježü kölčirgemüi keġegdemüi.
sentences.l: Mongols’ both men geldings land not-agreeing, plague-ill-are, is-said.
sentences.i: It is said that the Mongols, men and geldings alike, are falling sick, for the land does not agree with them.
sentences.n: The speaker passes on a report, as the Ming’s 被說有 ‘is said’ makes plain: keġegdemüi is keġe- ‘say’ + passive + present. ba ere aγta γažar (Ming 也 人 馬 地) is ‘both men, geldings, the land’. heġüšije- (Ming 不宜 ‘unsuitable’) and kölčirge- (Ming 瘟病 ‘plague, sickness’) are stems inferred from the Ming. The causal ‘for’ is mine, from the converb -žü after heġüši-.

morph.gloss: to disagree with, not suit (stem inferred from the Ming 不宜) [不宜着]
to fall sick, sicken (stem inferred from the Ming 瘟病) [瘟病了有]

sentences.t: Qān-a in-ü öki ögüje.
sentences.l: Qan-to his daughter let-us-give.
sentences.i: Let us give the Qan a daughter of the Altan Qan.
sentences.n: Ambiguous: in-ü is ‘his’ (Ming 他的), and the dative Qān-a (Ming 皇帝行) names the receiver, the Mongol Qan. I take ‘his’ as the Altan Qan’s own, and the unit below, in which a daughter named Güṅžü is brought out, supports that. ög- is ‘give’ with hortative -üje (Ming 與咱).

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; front-vowel form)

sentences.t: Altan Müṅgün aγ̇urasud ed čerig-ün küġün-e kündü-te γarγažu ögüje.
sentences.l: Gold silver silks goods army’s people-to heavily bringing-out let-us-give.
sentences.i: Let us bring out gold, silver, silks and goods and give them lavishly to the men of the army.
sentences.n: altan and müṅgün (Ming 金 銀) are the metals here, though altan is also the dynasty’s name. aγ̇urasud (Ming 段匹) are lengths of silk, with plural -d. kündü-te (Ming 重行) is hard: kündü is ‘heavy, weighty’, and the Ming’s 行 marks a dative. I read it as ‘heavily’, lavishly. But ‘to the weighty ones’, the chiefs, is possible. čerig-ün küġün-e is ‘to the army’s men’.

sentences.t: Ene eje-dür man-u oroqu ülüġü-ji ker medegdekü" keġen duradγaγ̇asu
sentences.l: "This counsel-in our following not-following-ACC how to-be-known" saying, if-he-reminded.
sentences.i: In this counsel, how can we tell who among us will go along and who will not?” When he had put it so,
sentences.n: I am not sure what is being asked. oroqu ülüġü-ji (Ming 從的 不從的 行) is ‘the ones who comply and the ones who do not’, and ker medegdekü (Ming 怎 可得知) ‘how can it be known’. It may mean that the plan to feign submission needs men whose loyalty can be told, but the text does not say so. ülüġü is odd (ülü ‘not’ + a noun ending); I follow the Ming. man-u is ‘our’, exclusive (Ming 俺的). Shiratori closes the Chancellor’s whole speech at medegdekü; keġen duradγaγ̇asu ‘when he had put it so’ follows.

morph.gloss: we, us (exclusive, oblique stem man-) [俺的]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
the not-so, those who do not (ülü ‘not’ + noun ending, uncertain) [不從的 行]
accusative: marks the object (after a vowel)
to bring to mind, mention, raise [提說呵]

sentences.t: Altan Qān Waṅgiṅ Čiṅsaṅ-un ene üge žöbšiježü "ein böġed boltuγai" keġen
sentences.l: Altan Qan Wangjing Chancellor’s this word approving, "thus indeed let-it-be" saying,
sentences.i: the Altan Qan approved this word of Chancellor Wangjing, and saying, “So be it,”
sentences.n: žöbšije- is ‘approve, say it is right’ (Ming 道是着; the glossary’s stem). ein böġed boltuγai is ‘thus, then, let it be’: ein (Ming 這般) ‘thus’, böġed (Ming 便) ‘then, just so’, boltuγai the third-person optative (Ming 者). Shiratori marks both ends of the Altan Qan’s words; `i` keeps them, in the form his marks give. Čiṅsaṅ-un is in the genitive, ‘of the Chancellor’, before ene üge ‘this word’.

morph.gloss: to approve, agree to (Ming 道是) [道是着]
ending: ‘being so, even so’; a particle of sequence, ‘and then’ (uncertain)
optative (third person): let it …, let them …

sentences.t: elsen Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-a Güṅžü neretei öki γarγažu
sentences.l: submitting, Chinggis Qaγan-to Gongzhu named daughter bringing-out,
sentences.i: and submitting, he brought out a daughter named Gongzhu for Chinggis Qahan,
sentences.n: Güṅžü is the Chinese word 公主, ‘princess’, and the Ming gives it no gloss: the girl’s title stands in for her name. neretei is nere ‘name’ + -tei (Ming 名字有的, ‘having the name’). γarγa- is ‘bring out’ (Ming 出着). The Qaγan-a ending is the dative (Ming 行). elsen opens the unit and continues the Altan Qan’s act from the one before.

morph.gloss: to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 歸附) [歸附]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: Altan müṅgün aγ̇urasun ed tabar čerig-ün küġün-e Küčün-e medeġülün daγ̇aqui-ača Žuṅdu-ača γarγažu
sentences.l: Gold silver silks goods property army’s people-to strength letting-know to-the-limit-of-bearing-from Zhongdu-from bringing-out,
sentences.i: and from Zhongdu he brought out gold, silver, silks and goods for the men of the army, each according to his strength, as much as they could carry,
sentences.n: Hard. küčün-e medeġülün daγ̇aqui-ača: küčün is ‘strength’ (Ming 氣力), medeġül- is ‘make known’ (Ming 敎知了), and daγ̇aqui-ača (Ming 儘力拿的行) is ‘from what (they) could bear, to the limit’. My ‘each according to his strength, as much as they could carry’ follows the Ming 儘力拿 ‘take to the limit of strength’. What exactly is made known, and by whom, is unclear. tabar (Ming 物) pairs with ed as ‘property’. Žuṅdu-ača is Zhongdu with the ablative, ‘from Zhongdu’.

morph.gloss: strength, power (the glossary’s küčü, stem küčün- before a case ending) [氣力行]
dative-locative: to, at (front-vowel form), after the n of the stem küčün-
to bear, endure, carry (a different sense from daγa- ‘follow’; stem uncertain) [儘力拿的行]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan-dur Waṅgiṅ-Žaṅsijaṅ kürgežü irebe.
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan-to Wangjing-Chancellor delivering came.
sentences.i: Chancellor Wangjing brought them and delivered them to Chinggis Qahan.
sentences.n: kürgežü is kürge- ‘bring to, deliver’ (kür- ‘reach’ made causative; Ming 送着), and irebe (Ming 來了) ‘came’. The Chancellor’s title is written here Žaṅsijaṅ, against Čiṅsaṅ above; the Han 丞相 stands behind Čiṅsaṅ, so they are taken as two spellings of one title.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
Wangjing the Chancellor (a name and a Chinese title) [人名]
to bring to, deliver (kür- ‘reach’ made causative; uncertain) [送着]

sentences.t: Elsen iregdežü Čiṅgis Qaγan eje-dür an-u orožu
sentences.l: Submission having-come-about, Chinggis Qaγan counsel-in his following,
sentences.i: When their submission had come about, Chinggis Qahan went along with his counsel,
sentences.n: Elsen iregdežü is ‘submission having been brought about’: ire- ‘come’ + passive -gde- (Ming 被來着). eje-dür an-u orožu (Ming 商量 裏 他的 從着) is ‘following his counsel’, an-u being the third-person genitive ‘his’, the Altan Qan’s. The capital on Elsen is Shiratori’s sentence start.

morph.gloss: to submit (stem inferred from the Ming 歸附) [歸附]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)

sentences.t: qotad qotad-tur eġered baγ̇uγsad čeriġüd-i qariγ̇ulžu ičuba.
sentences.l: cities, cities-in attacking those-who-took troops-ACC making-turn-back, withdrew.
sentences.i: had the troops that were attacking and taking city after city turn back, and withdrew.
sentences.n: baγ̇u- is ‘descend’, and with a city ‘bring down, take’ (the Ming’s 下 in 下的); eġered baγ̇uγsad is ‘having attacked, those who took’. qariγ̇ulžu is qari- ‘turn back’ + causative -γ̇ul-. Chinggis is the subject, carried from the unit before. ičuba, Ming 退了 ‘withdrew’.

morph.gloss: enclosure; walled town, city (compare qoton ‘pen’ in the glossary; here the Ming 城子) [城子每]
enclosure; walled town, city (compare qoton ‘pen’ in the glossary; here the Ming 城子) [城子每裏]
to descend, of a city, to take [下的(每)]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)
to withdraw, retreat (stem inferred; Ming 退) [退了]

sentences.t: Waṅgiṅ Čiṅsaṅ Možu, Füžü neretü qošiγ̇un-a kürtele Čiṅgis Qaγ̇an-i hüdežü qariba.
sentences.l: Wangjing Chancellor, Mozhou, Fuzhou named beak-to until, Chinggis Qaγan-ACC escorting, turned-back.
sentences.i: Chancellor Wangjing escorted Chinggis Qahan as far as the edge named Mozhou and Fuzhou, and turned back.
sentences.n: Možu and Füžü are two Chinese places (the Han write 莫州 and 撫州; the Ming says only 州名 and 郡名); neretü qošiγ̇un-a (Ming 名字有的 觜行) is ‘to the beak that has the name’, and I read ‘the edge named Mozhou and Fuzhou’, though why two names is not clear to me. hüde- is ‘escort, see off’ (Ming 送). The first word is printed as two, Waṅgiṅ Čiṅsaṅ, name and title (Ming 人名(官名)); the packet counts it as one word.

morph.gloss: Wangjing, a man’s name [人名(官名)]
Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
accusative: marks the object (after a consonant)

sentences.t: Aγ̇urasun ed bidan-u čeriġüd daγ̇aqui-ača ačižu kibuγ̇ud(i)-jar ačiγ̇a-ban tatažu jabuba.
sentences.l: Silks goods our troops to-the-limit loading, silk-with own-load binding went.
sentences.i: Our troops loaded the silks and goods, each as much as he could carry, bound their loads with silk, and marched away.
sentences.n: daγ̇aqui-ača (Ming 儘力) again means ‘to the limit of what they could carry’, now of the soldiers’ own loads. ači- is ‘load, carry on the back’ (Ming 䭾), and ačiγ̇a-ban ‘their own load’ (Ming 䭾 自的). kibuγ̇ud(i)-jar is kibuγ̇ud ‘silk’ (Ming 熟絹, ‘processed silk’) with the instrumental (Ming 敎), so the loads were tied with lengths of silk; that reading is mine. tata- is ‘pull’, here ‘pull tight, bind’ (Ming 縛着). jabuba (Ming 行了) is ‘went, marched’.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (after a vowel or the n of a stem; back-vowel form)
to bear, endure, carry (a different sense from daγa- ‘follow’; stem uncertain) [儘力]
to load, carry on the back [䭾着]
to pull, here, to bind tight [縛着]
